outlooks.summary: SCATTERED SEVERE STORMS WILL BE POSSIBLE FROM THE UPPER MIDWEST SOUTHWARD INTO PORTIONS OF THE CENTRAL PLAINS. MORE ISOLATED SEVERE STORMS WILL BE POSSIBLE OVER THE LOWER MISSISSIPPI AND TENNESSEE VALLEY REGION EASTWARD INTO THE CAROLINAS.

sections.title: THERE IS AN ENH RISK OF SVR TSTMS ACROSS PORTIONS OF MN/IA
sections.text: ...THERE IS A SLGT RISK OF SVR TSTMS ACROSS THE UPPER MIDWEST/MIDDLE MO VALLEY/CENTRAL PLAINS... ...THERE IS A MRGL RISK OF SVR TSTMS FROM THE CENTRAL/SOUTHERN HIGH PLAINS TO THE UPPER GREAT LAKES... ...THERE IS A MRGL RISK OF SVR TSTMS ACROSS THE TN VALLEY/SOUTHEAST STATES...

sections.title: EASTERN DAKOTAS/UPPER MIDWEST AND CENTRAL PLAINS
sections.text: A CLOSED UPPER LOW OVER EAST-CENTRAL MT THIS MORNING WILL CONTINUE TO ADVANCE NORTHEASTWARD TOWARD SOUTHERN SASKATCHEWAN/SOUTHWEST MANITOBA AND NORTHERN ND THROUGH TONIGHT...WHILE APPRECIABLE HEIGHT FALLS/FORCING FOR ASCENT WILL OVERSPREAD THE UPPER MIDWEST/MIDDLE MO VALLEY BY EVENING. IN THE WAKE OF A LATE SUNDAY/OVERNIGHT MCS...REGENERATIVE STORM DEVELOPMENT EARLY TODAY FROM THE ND/SD BORDER VICINITY EASTWARD INTO CENTRAL MN...AND RELATED OUTFLOW/CLOUD COVER...WILL BE CONSIDERABLE FACTORS FOR EFFECTIVELY DEFINING A WARM FRONT LATER TODAY...WHILE CASTING UNCERTAINTY REGARDING THE NORTHWARD EXTENT OF APPRECIABLE DESTABILIZATION ACROSS ND/NORTHERN MN INTO THIS AFTERNOON/EVENING. REGARDLESS...AS MASS RESPONSE OCCURS RELATED TO THE UPSTREAM TROUGH...THIS OUTFLOW/EFFECTIVE WARM FRONT SHOULD SHIFT POLEWARD AT LEAST TO SOME DEGREE IN ADVANCE OF AN EAST/NORTHEASTWARD-SPREADING COLD FRONT ACROSS THE EASTERN DAKOTAS/MN. INITIAL STRONG/SEVERE THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT THIS AFTERNOON APPEARS MOST PROBABLE NEAR/EAST OF WHERE THE COLD FRONT INTERSECTS THE RESIDUAL OUTFLOW/DIFFERENTIAL HEATING-RELATED WARM FRONT ACROSS MN...SOUTH-SOUTHWESTWARD INTO EASTERN NEB/WESTERN IA. AT LEAST SOME SEVERE RIS

sections.title: TN VALLEY/SOUTHEAST STATES
sections.text: WATER VAPOR IMAGERY FEATURES A WEAK/SLOW-MOVING MID-LEVEL LOW OVER THE MID-SOUTH THIS MORNING...WITH A RELATED MID-LEVEL COOL POCKET NOTED IN 12Z OBSERVED SOUNDINGS. SCATTERED STORMS ARE AGAIN EXPECTED DURING THE DAY WITH HEATING AND IN ASSOCIATION WITH THE SOMEWHAT COOL AIR ALOFT. STEEP LOW-LEVEL LAPSE RATES ALONG WITH AMPLE PRECIPITABLE WATER MAY ALLOW FOR A FEW STORM CLUSTERS CAPABLE OF LOCALIZED WIND DAMAGE THIS AFTERNOON/EARLY EVENING. ..GUYER/COHEN.. 07/11/2016

outlooks.summary: SCATTERED SEVERE STORMS WILL BE POSSIBLE FROM THE UPPER MIDWEST SOUTHWARD INTO PORTIONS OF THE CENTRAL PLAINS. MORE ISOLATED SEVERE STORMS WILL BE POSSIBLE FROM PARTS OF ALABAMA INTO THE CAROLINAS.

sections.title: ND/MN TO KS THROUGH TONIGHT
sections.text: THE PRIMARY SYNOPTIC CYCLONE WILL OCCLUDE OVER SE SK/SRN MB BY TONIGHT...WHILE A SECONDARY LOW OVER ERN SD DEVELOPS NNEWD IN ADVANCE OF THE SHORTWAVE TROUGH PROGRESSING EWD FROM THE NRN HIGH PLAINS. THE SURFACE PATTERN IS AGAIN COMPLICATED BY THE EFFECTS OF WIDESPREAD OVERNIGHT AND ONGOING CONVECTION...WITH A PRONOUNCED OUTFLOW BOUNDARY FROM SRN MN TO THE CYCLONE IN ERN SD. CONTINUED ELEVATED STORM DEVELOPMENT IN THE WAA REGIME ABOVE THE COLD POOL...THE REDUCTION IN LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE AND MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES WITH THE PRIOR CONVECTION...AND CONTINUED THICK CLOUD COVER ALL CAST CONSIDERABLE DOUBT ON THE POTENTIAL FOR DESTABILIZATION TODAY N OF THE OUTFLOW. SOME CLOUD BREAKS AND SURFACE HEATING MAY OCCUR ACROSS CENTRAL/ERN ND THIS AFTERNOON IMMEDIATELY IN ADVANCE OF THE SYNOPTIC FRONT...WHILE IT IS HIGHLY DOUBTFUL THAT PARTS OF N CENTRAL/NE MN WILL DESTABILIZE SUBSTANTIALLY. THE OUTFLOW BOUNDARY AND COLD FRONT MOVING SEWD ACROSS SD/NEB/KS WILL FOCUS THE PRIMARY SEVERE STORM THREATS THIS AFTERNOON INTO EARLY TONIGHT. THE REMAINING STEEP LAPSE RATE PLUME AND A WARM SECTOR WITH STRONG SURFACE HEATING AND BOUNDARY LAYER DEWPOINTS IN THE LOW 70S WILL RESULT IN A CORRIDOR OF STRONG BUOYANC

sections.title: MID SOUTH TO THE CAROLINAS THIS AFTERNOON
sections.text: A WEAK MIDLEVEL TROUGH REMAINS CENTERED OVER AR...WITH SMALLER-SCALE/WEAK MCV/S OVER NE MS AND WRN TN. MODIFIED 12Z SOUNDINGS SUGGEST LESS FAVORABLE PROFILES FOR WET MICROBURSTS /ESPECIALLY LOWER MS VALLEY/ AS A RESULT OF CONVECTIVE OVERTURNING THE PREVIOUS TWO DAYS. STILL...SUBSTANTIAL SURFACE HEATING AND BOUNDARY LAYER DEWPOINTS IN THE UPPER 60S TO LOWER 70S WILL BOOST MLCAPE TO 1500-2000 J/KG RANGE...AND ISOLATED STRONG OUTFLOW WINDS WILL BE POSSIBLE...PRIMARILY IN THE CORRIDOR FROM THE ONGOING CONVECTION IN SE AL NEWD TO THE STALLED FRONT IN THE CAROLINAS. ..THOMPSON/PICCA.. 07/11/2016

outlooks.summary: SCATTERED SEVERE STORMS ARE POSSIBLE FROM THE UPPER MIDWEST SOUTHWARD INTO PORTIONS OF THE CENTRAL AND SOUTHERN PLAINS. MORE ISOLATED SEVERE STORMS ARE POSSIBLE FROM PARTS OF ALABAMA INTO THE CAROLINAS. --- UPDATES ---

sections.title: UPPER MIDWEST TO SRN PLAINS
sections.text: ONLY SUBSTANTIAL ADJUSTMENT HAS BEEN TO UPGRADE TORNADO PROBABILITIES WITHIN CATEGORICAL SLGT RISK INVOF OUTFLOW BOUNDARY THAT WAS ANALYZED AT 19Z ACROSS S-CENTRAL MN AND E-CENTRAL SD. CONVECTIVE MODE OF STORMS INTERACTING WITH OUTFLOW BOUNDARY STILL IS IN QUESTION...HOWEVER ENVIRONMENTAL PARAMETER SPACE SUPPORTS RELATIVELY MAXIMIZED TORNADO POTENTIAL INVOF BOUNDARY WHETHER FROM SUPERCELLULAR OR QLCS FEATURES INVOLVED. THEREFORE HAVE INTRODUCED BOUNDARY-FOCUSED/SLGT-LEVEL TORNADO PROBABILITY BASED ON EXPECTED LATE-AFTN/EARLY EVENING COMBINATION OF LOWERED LCL ALONG/N OF BOUNDARY...CONTINUED DESTABILIZATION YIELDING 3000-4000 J/KG MLCAPE ALONG AND TO ITS S...RELATIVELY MAXIMIZED BOUNDARY-LAYER VORTICITY/SHEAR GIVEN BACKED NEAR-SFC FLOW...AND EFFECTIVE SRH 300-400 J/KG.

sections.title: SERN CONUS
sections.text: SCATTERED TO LOCALLY NUMEROUS TSTMS IN CLUSTERS HAVE DEVELOPED IN TWO PRIMARY AREAS RELATED TO PREVIOUS OUTLOOK...EACH OF WHICH STILL OFFERS POTENTIAL FOR DAMAGING DOWNDRAFTS AND ISOLATED SVR GUSTS -- CAROLINAS BORDER REGION MOVING GENERALLY EWD...AND SERN AL/SWRN GA REGION...MOVING NEWD. SEE SPC MESOSCALE DISCUSSIONS 1246-1247 FOR RECENT NEAR-TERM COVERAGE OF METEOROLOGICAL DETAILS FROM AL-CAROLINAS. ..EDWARDS.. 07/11/2016 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1130 AM CDT MON JUL 11 2016/

sections.text: A WEAK MIDLEVEL TROUGH REMAINS CENTERED OVER AR...WITH SMALLER-SCALE/WEAK MCV/S OVER NE MS AND WRN TN. MODIFIED 12Z SOUNDINGS SUGGEST LESS FAVORABLE PROFILES FOR WET MICROBURSTS /ESPECIALLY LOWER MS VALLEY/ AS A RESULT OF CONVECTIVE OVERTURNING THE PREVIOUS TWO DAYS. STILL...SUBSTANTIAL SURFACE HEATING AND BOUNDARY LAYER DEWPOINTS IN THE UPPER 60S TO LOWER 70S WILL BOOST MLCAPE TO 1500-2000 J/KG RANGE...AND ISOLATED STRONG OUTFLOW WINDS WILL BE POSSIBLE...PRIMARILY IN THE CORRIDOR FROM THE ONGOING CONVECTION IN SE AL NEWD TO THE STALLED FRONT IN THE CAROLINAS.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THUNDERSTORMS WILL CONTINUE TO DEVELOP EARLY THIS AFTERNOON...WITH SOME POTENTIAL FOR STRONG/MARGINALLY SEVERE WIND GUSTS. HOWEVER...THE THREAT FOR DAMAGING WINDS SHOULD REMAIN LOW ENOUGH TO PRECLUDE WATCH ISSUANCE.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: WITH SFC TEMPS RISING INTO THE UPPER 80S/LOWER 90S ACROSS MUCH OF SC AND SOUTH-CENTRAL NC...CONVECTION HAS BEGUN TO DEVELOP ACROSS THE REGION. MID-LEVEL FORCING FOR ASCENT IS RELATIVELY WEAK...BUT LOW-LEVEL CONVERGENCE ALONG A REMNANT OUTFLOW BOUNDARY AND STATIONARY FRONT SHOULD PROMOTE FURTHER INITIATION IN THIS UNCAPPED ENVIRONMENT. ADDITIONALLY...STORMS WILL CONTINUE TO ORGANIZE ACROSS THE HIGHER TERRAIN OF WESTERN SC/NC. DESPITE WEAK MID-LEVEL FLOW...PW VALUES UPWARDS OF 1.75-2 INCHES AND STEEP LOW-LEVEL LAPSE RATES WILL ENCOURAGE WET DOWNBURST POTENTIAL. ADDITIONALLY...VERY WEAK ANVIL-LEVEL FLOW MAY FAVOR THE FORMATION OF TRAILING STRATIFORM REGIONS WITH ANY UPSCALE GROWTH. SUCH FORMATION WOULD LOCALLY ENHANCE THE WIND THREAT AS CELLS GENERALLY HEAD EAST/SOUTHEAST TOWARDS THE COAST. NONETHELESS...A LACK OF WIDESPREAD CONVECTIVE ORGANIZATION SHOULD PRECLUDE WATCH ISSUANCE THIS AFTERNOON.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THUNDERSTORMS WILL CONTINUE TO BE CAPABLE OF ISOLATED STRONG/MARGINALLY SEVERE GUSTS THIS AFTERNOON. STORMS SHOULD GENERALLY REMAIN UNORGANIZED THOUGH...PRECLUDING WATCH ISSUANCE.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: CLUSTERS OF STRONG TO MARGINALLY SEVERE STORMS ARE SLOWLY PROGRESSING NORTH/NORTHEASTWARD ACROSS PARTS OF SOUTHERN AL/GA THIS AFTERNOON...AIDED BY LOW-LEVEL CONVERGENCE ALONG A SEA BREEZE AND MULTIPLE OUTFLOW BOUNDARIES. WITH NO CONVECTIVE INHIBITION PRESENT...CONTINUED STORM/OUTFLOW MERGERS SHOULD PROMOTE NEW CONVECTION...WITH AN OVERALL MOVEMENT OF THE CLUSTERS TO THE NORTHEAST. WEAK TROPOSPHERIC FLOW AND UNIMPRESSIVE MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES WILL LIMIT THE OVERALL THREAT FOR DAMAGING WINDS. HOWEVER...SFC TEMPS IN THE UPPER 80S TO LOWER 90S...ALONG WITH AMPLE MOISTURE /E.G. PW VALUES AROUND 1.75-2 INCHES/...WILL FAVOR OCCASIONAL WET DOWNBURSTS THIS AFTERNOON INTO EARLY EVENING.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: ONE OR TWO WATCHES WILL BE NEEDED THIS AFTERNOON INTO THE EVENING FROM CENTRAL/SOUTHERN MINNESOTA AND SOUTHEAST SOUTH DAKOTA SOUTHWARD THROUGH EASTERN PORTIONS OF NEBRASKA AND WESTERN IOWA. MUCH OF THIS AREA WILL TEND TO HAVE PRIMARILY STRONG TO SEVERE STORMS PRODUCING HAIL AND/OR DAMAGING WINDS...THOUGH THERE IS SOME POTENTIAL FOR A TORNADO THREAT ACROSS PART OF SOUTHERN MINNESOTA IN VICINITY OF A BOUNDARY EXTENDING FROM THE TWIN CITIES TO THE SOUTHWEST.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: SURFACE ANALYSES INTO THE EARLY-MID AFTERNOON SHOWED AN AREA OF LOW PRESSURE HAD SHIFTED EAST FROM CENTRAL TO EASTERN SD...AND WAS LOCATED NEAR KHON. AN OUTFLOW BOUNDARY ATTENDANT TO EARLY DAY TO AFTERNOON CONVECTION ACROSS CENTRAL MN HAS EVOLVED INTO A WARM FRONT AS STRONG SURFACE HEATING PERSISTS ACROSS SOUTHERN MN INTO SOUTHEAST SD. AT 20Z...THE WARM FRONT WAS ANALYZED FROM THE NORTH SIDE OF THE TWIN CITIES METRO AND WEST-SOUTHWESTWARD TO JUST NORTH OF KRWF INTO SOUTHEAST SD /NORTH OF KFSD/. MEANWHILE...A COLD FRONT WILL CONTINUE TO ADVANCE EAST INTO EASTERN NEBRASKA. MOISTENING AND HEATING OF THE WARM SECTOR THIS AFTERNOON HAS RESULTED IN MLCAPE RANGING FROM 2500-3500 J/KG. THIS COMBINED WITH STEEP MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES...HEIGHT FALLS AND STRENGTHENING MIDLEVEL WINDS/BULK SHEAR WILL SUPPORT ORGANIZED STORMS ALONG THE COLD FRONT. A TORNADO THREAT WILL BE GREATEST IN VICINITY OF THE WARM FRONT IN PART OF CENTRAL/SOUTHERN MN WHERE EFFECTIVE SRH WILL TEND TO REMAIN THE STRONGEST.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: ISOLATED STRONG TO SEVERE STORMS WILL BE POSSIBLE THROUGH THE LATE AFTERNOON INTO THE EVENING ACROSS CENTRAL PARTS OF NORTH DAKOTA AND NORTH-CENTRAL SOUTH DAKOTA. WW ISSUANCE IS UNLIKELY AT THIS TIME.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: THUNDERSTORMS HAVE BEEN INCREASING IN COVERAGE... GENERALLY SOUTH-NORTH ALONG WIND SHIFT AND LEADING EXTENT OF STRONGER FORCING FOR ASCENT WITH THE ATTENDANT CLOSED LOW/TROUGH LOCATED OVER THE NORTHERN HIGH PLAINS AND ADJACENT SOUTHERN SASKATCHEWAN. SURFACE-BASED INSTABILITY IS RELATIVELY WEAKER THAN LOCATIONS FARTHER TO THE SOUTHEAST...WITH MLCAPE RANGING FROM 500-1000 J/KG. THIS WILL BE THE MAIN LIMITING FACTOR FOR GREATER COVERAGE OF SEVERE STORMS...WHILE A BAND OF STRONG SWLY MIDLEVEL WINDS SPREADS FROM WESTERN SD INTO NORTH DAKOTA SUPPORTING STRONG BULK SHEAR. SHEAR VECTORS ORIENTED NEARLY PARALLEL TO THE INITIATING BOUNDARY SUGGESTS LINEAR STORM STRUCTURES WILL LIKELY PREVAIL. THESE FACTORS SUGGEST LOCALLY STRONG WINDS AND SOME HAIL WILL BE THE GREATEST SEVERE THREATS.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: TSTMS DEVELOPING NEAR A WARM FRONT ACROSS CNTRL MN INTO NWRN WI MAY POSE A LOCALIZED TORNADO THREAT...AND TRENDS ARE BEING MONITORED FOR A POSSIBLE SMALL TORNADO WATCH ACROSS THESE AREAS.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: RECENT RADAR TRENDS SHOW ISOLATED TSTMS DEVELOPING NEAR A WARM FRONT POSITIONED ACROSS CNTRL MN INTO NWRN WI...WITH A SUPERCELL NOW APPARENT ACROSS CHISAGO COUNTY MN ATTEMPTING TO BECOME ANCHORED ALONG THE BOUNDARY. SFC OBS SHOW THE MOST RAPID NWD MOVEMENT OF THE WARM FRONT IS OCCURRING ACROSS NWRN WI...WHILE OUTFLOW/PRECIPITATION ACROSS PARTS OF NRN/CNTRL MN IS REINFORCING COOLER AIR MORE EFFECTIVELY N OF THE BOUNDARY. VWP DATA FROM MPX SAMPLED STRONG LOW-LEVEL FLOW SUPPORTING A CURVED HODOGRAPH IN THE LOWEST SEVERAL KM AGL...AND AUGMENTING THE SFC WIND PROFILE FOR ELY WINDS N OF THE BOUNDARY WILL BE FAVORABLE KINEMATICALLY FOR A TORNADO THREAT. TRENDS ARE BEING MONITORED FOR ISSUANCE OF A SMALL TORNADO WATCH FOR PARTS OF CNTRL MN INTO NWRN WI...AND THIS MAY REPLACE PORTIONS OF SVR TSTM WATCH 372.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: DMGG WIND POTENTIAL APPEARS TO BE INCREASING IN ASSOCIATION WITH A BOWING LINE SEGMENT MOVING ACROSS NWRN WI. A WATCH WILL LIKELY BE ISSUED SOON.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: RECENT RADAR TRENDS SHOW A SMALL BOWING LINE WITH EMBEDDED CIRCULATIONS EVOLVING OUT OF PERSISTENT AREA OF CONVECTION ACROSS NRN MN...AND EWD MOTION IS CURRENTLY ESTIMATED AT 40 KT. MEANWHILE...A WARM FRONT HAS PROGRESSED NWD INTO NRN WI...WITH SFC TEMPERATURES IN THE 80S F AMIDST LOW 70S F DEWPOINTS YIELDING MLCAPE VALUES NEAR 2000 J/KG IMMEDIATELY S OF THE FRONT. MID-UPPER FLOW WEAKENS SUBSTANTIALLY WITH EWD PROGRESSION...BUT 30-40 KT OF OBSERVED FLOW IN THE LOWEST 3 KM AGL /PER REGIONAL VWP DATA/ COMBINED WITH THE DESTABILIZING AIR MASS DOWNSHEAR FROM THE BOWING LINE WILL SUPPORT A STRONG TO DMGG WIND THREAT ACROSS NRN WI INTO THE WRN U.P. OF MI. A WATCH WILL LIKELY BE ISSUED SOON.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THE SEVERE THREAT CONTINUES ACROSS WW 373.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: SCATTERED CONVECTION HAS DEVELOPED ALONG NORTHERN PORTIONS OF WW 373 /ACROSS STANTON AND CUMING COUNTIES IN NEBRASKA/...WITH MORE ISOLATED CONVECTION SOUTH ALONG A COLD FRONT THAT STRETCHES FROM NEAR HSI SOUTHWESTWARD TO NEAR GCK. THIS COLD FRONT WILL SERVE AS AN INITIATING BOUNDARY FOR CONTINUED CONVECTION IN THE WATCH AREA...AND A MORE CONDITIONAL THREAT FOR STORMS WILL EXIST ALONG THE FRONT SOUTHWEST OF THE WATCH INTO CENTRAL/WEST-CENTRAL KANSAS AS INCREASED LOW-LEVEL CONVERGENCE DEVELOPS IN RESPONSE TO AN INCREASING LOW-LEVEL JET ACROSS THE REGION. MODERATE TO STRONG INSTABILITY AND 30-40 KNOT DEEP SHEAR /WEAKER WITH SOUTHWARD EXTENT/ WILL SUSTAIN THE STORMS AND SUPPORT A SEVERE WIND/HAIL THREAT THROUGH AT LEAST 03Z.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: TSTM COVERAGE IS SLOWLY INCREASING ACROSS WRN IA...AND A THREAT FOR MARGINALLY SVR HAIL AND DMGG WIND GUSTS CONTINUES. A NEW WATCH MAY BE NEEDED BY 03Z TO ACCOUNT FOR A POSSIBLE DMGG WIND THREAT ACROSS WRN/CNTRL IA AND S-CNTRL MN.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: TSTMS HAVE GRADUALLY INCREASED IN COVERAGE/INTENSITY ACROSS WRN IA WITHIN BROAD/WEAK CONFLUENCE ZONE AND LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE AXIS... AHEAD OF A PRE-FRONTAL TROUGH...WITH DMGG WINDS AND MARGINALLY SVR HAIL POSSIBLE. RECENT RADAR LOOP SHOWS A CLUSTER OF TSTMS CROSSING THE MO VALLEY BEGINNING TO ACCELERATE EWD...AND BOTH OBSERVATIONAL AND CONVECTION-ALLOWING MODEL TRENDS SUGGEST INTERACTIONS/MERGERS WITH NEIGHBORING STORMS TO THE N COULD RESULT IN UPSCALE GROWTH TO A MCS ACROSS WRN/CNTRL IA. SHOULD THESE TRENDS CONTINUE...DMGG WIND THREAT WOULD LIKELY INCREASE AND SPREAD EWD TOWARDS THE ERN EDGE OF WATCHES 372/373...AND A NEW DOWNSTREAM WATCH FOR WRN/CNTRL IA AND SOUTH-CENTRAL MN MAY BE CONSIDERED CLOSE TO EXPIRATION TIME OF 03Z.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THE POTENTIAL FOR A BRIEF TORNADO...STRONG WIND GUSTS...AND MARGINALLY SVR HAIL CONTINUES WITH DEVELOPING TSTMS ALONG/S OF A STALLED FRONT ACROSS CNTRL MN. THESE THREATS SHOULD GRADUALLY DECREASE THROUGH 03Z...AND A NEW WW IS NOT CURRENTLY ANTICIPATED.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: LATEST SFC OBS SHOW A WARM FRONT HAS NEARLY STALLED ACROSS CNTRL MN...AS PERSISTENT AREA OF CONVECTION HAS REINFORCED COOL TEMPERATURES/OUTFLOW TO THE N. MORE RECENTLY...DEVELOPING TSTMS ACROSS CNTRL MN HAVE OCCASIONALLY EXHIBITED ROTATION...AND A TORNADO OR TWO REMAIN POSSIBLE GIVEN STRONG LOW-LEVEL WIND FIELDS OBSERVED IN MPX VWP DATA. HOWEVER...TSTMS ARE DEVELOPING NEAR THE STALLED FRONT AND QUICKLY BECOMING ELEVATED AS THEY MOVE NWD...WITH A LIMITED SPATIOTEMPORAL WINDOW FOR A TORNADO THREAT. RECENT CONVECTIVE TRENDS SUGGEST THIS THREAT WILL BE CONFINED TO ERN PORTIONS OF TORNADO WATCH 374 /N OF THE MINNEAPOLIS AREA/ FOR THE NEXT HR OR SO...BUT WITH HEAVY RAIN BECOMING THE DOMINANT THREAT...A NEW WW IS NOT CURRENTLY ANTICIPATED. ..ROGERS.. 07/12/2016 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: AN ISOLATED THREAT FOR LARGE HAIL AND STRONG WIND GUSTS WILL DEVELOP ACROSS PARTS OF CNTRL/ERN KS AND FAR SERN NEB THROUGH THE EARLY MORNING. A WATCH IS NOT CURRENTLY ANTICIPATED...BUT TRENDS ARE BEING MONITORED.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: RADAR TRENDS SHOW AN INCREASE IN TSTMS ACROSS CNTRL KS OVER THE PAST HR...WHICH MAY BE PARTIALLY ENHANCED BY A 40-50 KT LLJ NOW PRESENT OVER OK AND SRN KS. ADDITIONAL ISOLATED TSTMS HAVE ALSO FORMED ALONG/NEAR A COLD FRONT ENTERING N-CNTRL KS...AND ONE SUCH TSTM OVER RUSSELL COUNTY KS /AS OF 350Z/ IS EXHIBITING THE POTENTIAL FOR LARGE HAIL. 12/00Z SOUNDINGS FROM TOP/LMN SHOW AN INVERSION NEAR 2 KM AGL...AND DEVELOPING TSTMS MAY BE PRIMARILY ELEVATED. ONE EXCEPTION MAY BE ALONG THE COLD FRONT...WHERE LOW-LEVEL FORCING FOR ASCENT IS STRONGER...AND MORE WIDESPREAD DEVELOPMENT COULD LEAD TO A FEW CLUSTERS OR LINE SEGMENTS EVOLVING. THE PRESENCE OF VERY STEEP MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES IS YIELDING WIDESPREAD MUCAPE VALUES OF 2000-3000 J/KG...SUFFICIENT FOR AN ISOLATED THREAT FOR LARGE HAIL AND STRONG WIND GUSTS. HOWEVER...IT IS UNCERTAIN WHETHER COVERAGE OF THESE THREATS WILL WARRANT A WATCH...BUT TRENDS WILL BE MONITORED.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: SOME INCREASE IN STRONG SURFACE GUSTS APPEARS POSSIBLE NEAR THE I-70 CORRIDOR FROM TOPEKA INTO KANSAS CITY DURING THE NEXT FEW HOURS. IT IS NOT YET CLEAR THAT A WATCH IS NEEDED...BUT TRENDS ARE BEING MONITORED FOR THIS POSSIBILITY.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: FORCING FOR ASCENT ALONG SOUTHWARD AND EASTWARD ADVANCING COLD POOLS IS MAINTAINING VIGOROUS THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT...MAINLY ACROSS PARTS OF NORTHEASTERN KANSAS AND NORTHWEST MISSOURI. THIS IS OCCURRING DESPITE A CONTINUED GRADUAL INCREASE IN INHIBITION FOR SEASONABLY MOIST BOUNDARY LAYER PARCELS...BENEATH WARM ELEVATED MIXED LAYER AIR. HOWEVER...WITH FORCED LIFT THROUGH THE MID-LEVEL INHIBITION...LARGE CAPE IS BEING REALIZED. WESTERLY MID/UPPER FLOW ACROSS THE LOWER CENTRAL PLAINS INTO LOWER MISSOURI VALLEY IS RATHER WEAK...BUT SOUTHWESTERLY LOW-LEVEL FLOW ...ASSOCIATED WITH THE NOCTURNALLY ENHANCED LOW-LEVEL JET...IS ON THE ORDER OF 40-50+ KT. HEAVY PRECIPITATION LOADING AND DOWNWARD TRANSFER OF THIS MOMENTUM APPEARS TO HAVE CONTRIBUTED TO RECENT SCATTERED SEVERE WIND GUSTS. ALTHOUGH THE LOW-LEVEL JET IS PAST ITS DIURNAL PEAK...AND WILL COMMENCE MORE SUBSTANTIVE WEAKENING THROUGH THE 09-12Z TIME FRAME ...AT LOCALIZED STRONG TO SEVERE SURFACE GUSTS PROBABLY WILL CONTINUE ANOTHER COUPLE OF HOURS. CONTINUED UPSCALE GROWTH OF CONVECTION NOW OCCURRING NEAR/NORTHWEST OF TOPEKA DOES NOT APPEAR OUT OF THE QUESTION. THIS APPEARS NEAR THE INTERSECTION OF THE SOUTHWARD AND EASTWARD ADVANCING OUTFLOWS...AND COULD CONTINUE EASTWARD ALONG THE SOUTHWARD ADVANCING OUTFLOW INTO PORTIONS OF THE KANSAS CITY METRO AREA DURING THE 10-12Z TIME FRAME...WITH PERHAPS INCREASING ORGANIZATION. THIS SEEMS TO PROVIDE THE BEST CHANCE FOR SUSTAINED STRONG SURFACE GUSTS THROUGH THE EARLY MORNING DAYLIGHT HOURS.
